thread:
noah: Hey team, seeing a spike of 502/504s from hosted inference starting ~10:15 PDT. customer request ids: trace=ff12a4, ff12b9. All in us-west. Can you help?
jordan (Support): Thanks @noah — can you paste a sample request id and any repro steps? are they consistent for one customer or wide?
noah: sample trace ff12a4, happens for both chat and completion endpoints. Customer says ~20% of calls fail during bursts. No schema changes on their side.
amy (SRE): looking at edge logs for us-west. I see a sudden bump in upstream 502s to inference-router between 10:14:45 and 10:18:30. Envoy shows `upstream reset` and `stream idle timeout` entries. Initial thought: h2 connection pool exhaustion or upstream auth latency.
ops-bot: Deploy bot: Automated canary deploy finished at 09:50 — no new deploys between 09:50 and 11:00.
sudhir (Eng): Did any billing header rollout happen? We had a header injection experiment yesterday that caused larger-than-normal headers for some clients.
maria (Platform): Yep, billing header feature flag `x-cust-billing-v2` was enabled for select cohorts at 09:00. It adds a ~2kb header for enterprise tenants. Could that push us over header size limits and cause upstream resets?
amy (SRE): possible. Envoy logs show `413` for very large headers, but majority are 502/504 where upstream closed stream. I also see `HTTP/2 stream error: REFUSED_STREAM` in a subset.
alex (Oncall): I'm running a targeted tail on the edge pod logs and the inference-router pod. Sample envoy excerpt:
```
[2024-11-02T10:15:01Z] "POST /v1/generate" 502 - upstream_reset_before_response_duration_ms=12 route=hosted-inference
"upstream error: stream closed by peer" peer=10.2.18.45:443
```
So upstream TLS connection reset. Under high concurrency we might hit connection pool limits and then upstreams drop.
jordan (Support): Customer provided cURL for repro:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-xxx" \
  -H "x-cust-billing-v2: <long-b64-payload>" -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
amy (SRE): repro locally with a few concurrent requests using their header, I can repro ~10% 502s when concurrency >=16. Without the header it's fine. So header seems to increase per-connection resource usage and exposes connection pool exhaustion.
sudhir (Eng): Two mitigations: 1) temporarily route flagged customers to a larger upstream pool (more connections) 2) add `max_request_headers_kb` increase on the inference-router Envoy cluster to avoid 413s and reduce errant resets. Also consider trimming/encoding the header.
maria (Platform): For immediate mitigation, I've pushed a routing rule to send requests with `x-cust-billing-v2` to the `large-header-pool` nodes (higher max_conns) in us-west. This should reduce failures while we roll a config change.
ops-bot: Config change deployed to edge-router-us-west @ 10:35 by maria. Rolling update started.
alex (Oncall): After the routing change, failure rate dropped from 18% -> 3% in the next 5 minutes. Still seeing occasional 504s for long-tail requests (~1-2%).
noah: Great, customer reporting improvement. They still see occasional timeouts on bursts of 1000 concurrent requests.
amy (SRE): Added tracing: the 504s correlate with auth backend latency spikes (auth service p95 spiked to 800ms at 10:16). When auth is slow, Envoy waits and then fails the stream. I'll open a ticket with auth team and pin traces.
sudhir (Eng): Auth team confirmed a garbage collection pause in their Go service due to a large batch job at 10:14. They are patching the job and adding a circuit breaker in front of the auth cluster.
jordan (Support): Summary so far for the customer: cause = combination of large billing header increasing connection utilization + intermittent auth backend latency. Mitigations applied: routing flagged customers to large-header pool (done) + auth team patching GC job + follow-up config to increase connection pool and header size limits (planned).
noah: Thanks. Any recommended customer workaround? They can remove the long header but would prefer it for billing telemetry.
sudhir (Eng): Short-term workaround: batch calls or use lower concurrency bursts; longer-term: we'll add header compression on the proxy and better connection scaling.
amy (SRE): Follow-ups I'm filing:
- Increase `max_request_headers_kb` from 96 -> 128 on inference-router clusters (PR opened #2345)
- Add explicit `priority`/`pool` route for large-header clients across regions
- Add graceful fallback: if upstream auth exceeds 500ms, skip non-essential header verification and default to cached auth token (config PR #2346)
- Postmortem if recurrence
tier2-support-bot: Created support case #SUP-2024-718 with root cause draft. Linking to customer workspace and traces.
maria (Platform): I'll monitor error budget impact and roll the header size change at 03:00 UTC if no regressions. For now leaving the routing rule in place.
alex (Oncall): Marking incident as mitigated. Will continue to watch for 24h. Reopen if error rate >5% for >15m.
noah: Customer says thank you, improvement is visible. Please keep me in the loop.
jordan (Support): Will send the customer a short write-up + mitigation timeline. Closing thread once PRs merge and auth patch verified.
amy (SRE): Adding reproducible steps to internal wiki: reproduce with `hey` or `wrk` to generate concurrency >=16 with header present. Example command:
```
hey -n 1000 -c 20 -H "x-cust-billing-v2: <long-payload>" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-xxx" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
End of thread.
